title: Ref chief Webb backs process around Yoro sending off despite successful appeal
summary: In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb analyses Man Utd defender Leny Yoro's sending off vs Liverpool - now  overturned on appeal - as audio of how the o
content:
In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb analyses Man Utd defender Leny Yoro's sending off vs Liverpool - now overturned on appeal - as audio of how the officials handled the incident in real time is revealed Referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the process of the officials who sent off Manchester United defender Leny Yoro at Liverpool - despite the red card being overturned on appeal.

Yoro, sent off after eight minutes of Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield, was due to face a one-match ban for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity when he brought down Alexander Isak outside the box and he was in on goal.

However, United have had the suspension lifted after a successful claim of wrongful dismissal, the FA said on Tuesday.

The independent commission will publish the written reasons in "due course".

In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb, chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, described the on-field decision from referee Samuel Barrott as "decisive" and said the point of contention was around whether Isak would beat United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to the ball.

summary:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak
Manchester United reporter in LisbonPublished24 November 2026, 15:59 GMTUpdated 32 minutes agoThe Football Assoc
content:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak Manchester United reporter in LisbonPublished24 November 2026, 15:59 GMTUpdated 32 minutes agoThe Football Association has overturned Leny Yoro's red card from Manchester United's defeat by Liverpool on Sunday – even though referee's chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.

Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into the Anfield clash.

Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch which meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if the Liverpool man had not been brought down by Yoro just outside the area.

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at the decision, which, he felt, changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.

"The ball wasn't in his control," he said.

Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 in the final in January, but were stripped of the title by a Confederation of African Football (CAF) Appeal Board in March for breaking competition rules by walking off the pitch because of a late disallowed goal and a controversial penalty award.

content:

The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.

The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them.

Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to Cas, sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October.

Image source, ShutterstockImage caption, Millwall, who are 16th in the Championship, have average league gates of 19,418 at The Den this season Millwall have been ordered to play a future Championship match in front of a partially-closed stadium as punishment for fans' discriminatory chants.

The club has also been fined £70,000 by an independent regulatory commission, and been told another offence this season will lead to a further partial stadium closure.

The sanctions were imposed for ableist and homophobic chants, heard at a game against Charlton Athletic in January.

"These chants are discriminatory, unacceptable, and will not be tolerated at The Den or anywhere Millwall play," Millwall's managing director Mark Fairbrother said in an open letter to supporters., external "The club condemns them without reservation.

They do not represent this club, and the vast majority of supporters who follow Millwall home and away with passion and pride.

title: Bayern hold constructive talks with Musiala's representatives amid ongoing tensions
summary: Following weeks of public debate surrounding Jamal Musiala's health and contractual situation, Bayern Munich have taken a step towards easing tensions with the German international's entourage. As per Sky Germa
content:
Following weeks of public debate surrounding Jamal Musiala's health and contractual situation, Bayern Munich have taken a step towards easing tensions with the German international's entourage.

As per Sky Germany, Musiala's agents Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschäffl met with Jan-Christian Dreesen, Herbert Hainer and Max Eberl at Säbener Straße on Tuesday, with neither Uli Hoeneß nor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge - both of whom have publicly raised concerns over Musiala's situation in recent weeks - present at the meeting.

The discussions are said to have been constructive, with both parties keen to improve communication behind closed doors following the recent public exchanges.

Having made his return to action against Köln on Friday, it is said that Musiala will now be given time to focus on his football, with the Bayern hierarchy keen to alleviate some of the pressure on the 23-year-old.

In the meantime, the attacking midfielder may have to take on a more integral role, with Harry Kane's absence, the unavailability of Michael Olise, and doubts over Luis Diaz ahead of the trip to Lille on Wednesday.

summary: PISA, ITALY - MAY 17: Antonio Conte manager of SSC Napoli looks on during the Serie A match between Pisa SC and SSC Napoli at Arena Garibaldi on May 17, 2026 in Pisa, Italy. (Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Im
content:
PISA, ITALY - MAY 17: Antonio Conte manager of SSC Napoli looks on during the Serie A match between Pisa SC and SSC Napoli at Arena Garibaldi on May 17, 2026 in Pisa, Italy.

(Photo by Gabriele Maltinti/Getty Images) Antonio Conte’s recent interview has fuelled speculation of a return to Juventus, but the Bianconeri might have other ideas if Luciano Spalletti leaves.

Conte is undoubtedly part of Juventus’ history, both as a player and as a coach.

A serial Serie A champion and a 1996 Champions League winner with the Old Lady, Conte left his mark in Turin also as a coach, winning the first three Scudetti in the post-Calciopoli era.
